title: Eliminating a split unit group on monomial ideal tensors
statement:
Let $Q$ be a commutative monoid written additively, $G$ an abelian group, $A$ a commutative ring, $c:Q\to(A,\cdot)$ a monoid homomorphism, and $v:G\to A^\times$ a homomorphism. For a monoid ideal $K\subset Q$ (that is, $K+Q\subset K$, allowing $\varnothing$), put $L=K\oplus G\subset Q\oplus G$. For any ring $D$ and monoid $T$, $D[T]$ is the ring of finite sums of monomials $d_tz^t$ with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$, and $D[K]$ denotes the ideal additively spanned by its indicated monomials. Give $A$ its $\mathbf Z[Q\oplus G]$-algebra structure $z^{(q,g)}\mapsto c(q)v(g)$, and write $A_c$ for the $\mathbf Z[Q]$-module with action $z^q\mapsto c(q)$.
The extension of $\mathbf Z[K]$ along $\mathbf Z[Q]\to\mathbf Z[Q\oplus G]$, $z^q\mapsto z^{(q,0)}$, is $\mathbf Z[L]$. There is an $A$-linear isomorphism of module tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]
$$\sigma:\mathbf Z[L]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[Q\oplus G]}A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf Z[K]\otimes_{\mathbf Z[Q]}A_c,\qquad z^{(q,g)}\otimes a\longmapsto z^q\otimes v(g)a,$$
with inverse $z^q\otimes a\mapsto z^{(q,0)}\otimes a$. If $\mu_L$ and $\mu_K$ are multiplication to $A$, so $\mu_L(z^{(q,g)}\otimes a)=c(q)v(g)a$ and $\mu_K(z^q\otimes a)=c(q)a$, then $\mu_K\sigma=\mu_L$. The inverse of $\sigma$ is precisely the ideal-tensor map induced by the displayed inclusion of monoid rings and the identity on $A$. These maps commute with coefficient homomorphisms $\phi:A\to A'$ carrying $c,v$ to the chosen new characters.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z[Q]$, $S=\mathbf Z[Q\oplus G]$, $I=\mathbf Z[K]$, and $J=\mathbf Z[K\oplus G]$. The additive span $J$ is an ideal: multiplying $z^{(q,g)}$, $q\in K$, by $z^{(r,h)}$ gives $z^{(q+r,g+h)}$ with $q+r\in K$. It contains the image of $I$, so $IS\subset J$. Conversely every spanning monomial satisfies $z^{(q,g)}=z^{(q,0)}z^{(0,g)}\in IS$, so $J=IS$. This proves ideal extension as an equality of ideals, without asserting injectivity of any tensor multiplication map.

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75, split chart; VIII 3.4.2--3.4.3, printed p. 110, monoidal ideals. Agent finite-monomial calculation.

proof.text: Write $N=I\otimes_R A_c$, with its $A$-action on the second factor and hence its $S$-action through $z^{(r,h)}\mapsto c(r)v(h)$. On the additive monomial basis of $J$ define $B(z^{(q,g)},a)=z^q\otimes v(g)a$, extending by integer linearity in $J$ and additivity in $a$. For $r\in Q,h\in G$, tensor balancing in $N$ gives $B(z^{(q+r,g+h)},a)=z^{q+r}\otimes v(g)v(h)a=z^q\otimes c(r)v(g)v(h)a=B(z^{(q,g)},c(r)v(h)a)$. The same expression is $z^{(r,h)}B(z^{(q,g)},a)$. Finite expansion extends both linearity identities to every element of $S$, so $B$ is $S$-bilinear. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $\sigma:J\otimes_S A\to N$ with the claimed formula. Since $B(x,ba)=bB(x,a)$, uniqueness also gives $A$-linearity. Apply [lem-trf-monomial-ideal-tensor-presentation] to the family indexed by K times G; its single balancing equation supplies the A-linear forward map.

proof.text: Define $C(z^q,a)=z^{(q,0)}\otimes a$ in $J\otimes_S A$, extending by integer linearity and additivity. For $r\in Q$, $C(z^{q+r},a)=z^{(q+r,0)}\otimes a=z^{(q,0)}\otimes c(r)a=C(z^q,c(r)a)$; this also equals the $z^r$-action on $C(z^q,a)$. Thus $C$ is $R$-bilinear. By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] it induces $\tau:N\to J\otimes_S A$, and $C(x,ba)=bC(x,a)$ makes $\tau$ $A$-linear. The map $I\to J$, $z^q\mapsto z^{(q,0)}$, and the identity on $A$ give exactly this formula, so $\tau$ is the specified ideal-tensor map. In Lean, construct this canonical inverse directly as a semilinear TensorProduct.map along the ring inclusion; its coefficient component is the identity.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product: universal property and bilinearity relations; explicit agent calculation in the split-chart context of ILO Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75, and VIII 3.4.3, printed p. 110.

proof.text: On a monomial pure tensor, $\sigma\tau(z^q\otimes a)=z^q\otimes v(0)a=z^q\otimes a$. In the other direction, $\tau\sigma(z^{(q,g)}\otimes a)=z^{(q,0)}\otimes v(g)a=z^{(q,0)}z^{(0,g)}\otimes a=z^{(q,g)}\otimes a$ by $S$-balancing. Pure tensors generate by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; expanding their first factors into finite monomial sums and moving integer coefficients to the second factor shows that these monomial pure tensors generate as $A$-modules. Both composites are therefore identities, giving the claimed isomorphism and inverse. The additive extensionality theorem of [lem-trf-monomial-ideal-tensor-presentation] is applied to both composites.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product: universal property and bilinearity relations; explicit agent calculation in the split-chart context of ILO Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75, and VIII 3.4.3, printed p. 110.

proof.text: The evaluations $I\to A$, $z^q\mapsto c(q)$, and $J\to A$, $z^{(q,g)}\mapsto c(q)v(g)$, are respectively $R$-linear and $S$-linear, since $c(q+r)=c(q)c(r)$ and $v(g+h)=v(g)v(h)$. Multiplication by the second factor therefore induces the displayed $\mu_K,\mu_L$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On $z^{(q,g)}\otimes a$, $\mu_K\sigma$ and $\mu_L$ both give $c(q)v(g)a$, proving their equality on generators. For $\phi:A\to A\prime$, let $c\prime=\phi c$ and $v\prime=\phi v$. The coefficient maps on the two tensors send $z^{(q,g)}\otimes a$ and $z^q\otimes a$ to the same monomials tensored with $\phi(a)$; bilinearity makes them well defined. Applying $\sigma\prime$ after coefficient change gives $z^q\otimes v\prime(g)\phi(a)=z^q\otimes\phi(v(g)a)$, exactly coefficient change after $\sigma$. For $\tau$ both orders give $z^{(q,0)}\otimes\phi(a)$; for multiplication both orders give $\phi(c(q)v(g)a)$ (and $\phi(c(q)a)$ for $K$). Generation proves all asserted naturality identities. The multiplication identity is checked by [lem-trf-monomial-ideal-tensor-presentation]. Coefficient change is a TensorProduct.map; prove the inverse square on arbitrary pure tensors from its inclusion formula, and deduce the forward square by the two inverse identities.
